segments.label: Short 1 card
I've learned to not predict
segments.status: MINED 2026-11-21 (VTT 00:45:28 to 00:46:04; trim to breath in cutroom); the twin s11a carries it
segments.quote_anchor: I've learned to not predict, not have a directional bias. I've learned to take the emotional loss of the complete trade at the moment of entry ... any exit that's better than a loss of the whole position is still a positive feeling for me. So I've learned to incorporate my monkey nature and my emotions in that way, and that allows me to be systematic.
segments.why: The single best hook on tape: the react-not-predict idea in his own sentence, ending on 'systematic'.

segments.label: Short 2 card
Waiting for my wife, I found Van Tharp's book
segments.status: MINED 2026-11-21 (VTT 00:11:49 to 00:12:19); the twin s21a carries it
segments.quote_anchor: somehow I was in a bookstore waiting for my wife and I saw Van Tharp's book, Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom ... two hours later she comes and finds me, says let's go, and I found that his combination of psychology, statistics and finding your edge and personalizing it really resonated with me a lot
segments.why: The hook: a human story before any credential.

segments.label: Short 3 card
The night he could not sleep
segments.status: MINED 2026-11-21 (VTT 01:01:07 to 01:01:44); the twin s31a carries it
segments.quote_anchor: my existential moment was when my dad, who trusted me beyond all reason ... I had his entire retirement account in a position because I thought it was going to go up tomorrow ... I've got more than 100 percent of his retirement in that position and I couldn't sleep the rest of the night, and what I learned was that I have to make long-term decisions based on my pessimistic nature
segments.why: The most human moment on tape and the origin of his sizing rule.

segments.label: Every decision through the pessimistic mind; that's why I became a systematic trader
segments.status: MINED 2026-11-21 (VTT 01:02:16 to 01:02:53); the twin s32a carries it
segments.quote_anchor: every important decision I've ever made had to go through the lens of the pessimistic mind and be satisfied that I understood the maximum adverse consequence, what is the worst thing that could possibly happen, and then if I can live with that then I could proceed ... and that's why I became a systematic trader
segments.why: The lesson, ending on the word the whole channel is about.
